newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares driven higher by Lek.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares driven higher by Lek.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed 0.38 percent higher on Thursday, pushed up by a three percent rise in market heavyweight drug maker Lek.
"Lek probably rose today in expectation of a dividend pay-out," said Mateja Gubanec, a broker of A bank.
The SBI index added on 0.38 percent or 4.97 points to 1,322.37.
Brokers said market direction depends on whether Slovenia ratifies the EU association accord, signed in June last year.

"By the end of next week shares could move around three percent either way largely depending on news regarding the EU asociation accord. A ratification would significantly improve liquidity," Gubanec said.
Parliament is expected to vote within the next two weeks on whether to ratify the agreement.
Overall 11 shares rose, two fell and one was flat, while 14 were untraded. Turnover rose to 65.1 million tolars from 55.2 million tolars.
Issue A of drug maker Lek was the most active share, rising 3.02 percent to 24,900 tolars on volume of 576 shares for total turnover of 13.9 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the top gainer, jumping 4.15 percent to 4,999 tolars on volume of 15 shares.
Food processing company Droga led the day's decliners, easing 1.69 percent to 29,000 tolars on volume of 90 shares.
Slovenia's second largest bank SKB, which said it would buy 51 percent of listed bank UBK, rose 0.45 percent to 49,170 tolars on volume of 51 shares, while UBK was untraded.
